title: AI detector unavailable counter is incremented only on the retry-exhausted path
answers: Why does the ai detector checks unavailable metric count more than once per check?
AI detector check failure counted once per Temporal attempt
body:
`posthog_insight_alerts_ai_detector_checks_total{outcome="unavailable"}` must be one increment per scheduled check, not per Temporal attempt.
- Enforced in `posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:record_failed_evaluation` (`_record`): increments only when `error.get("code") == LLM_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR_CODE` AND an errored check was actually written.
- `evaluate_alert`/`_evaluate` must NOT call `record_ai_detector_check_outcome("unavailable")` when re-raising `LLMDetectorUnavailableError`; a retry that then succeeds would otherwise count both failure and success.
- Early returns in `_record` (alert disabled, gone, or `next_check_at` in the future) write no errored check and so must not move the counter.
- Tests: `test_an_unavailable_detector_is_not_counted_on_every_attempt`, `test_counts_one_unavailable_outcome_per_recorded_failure` in `posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_activities.py`.
applies: Alert Temporal activities and AI detector health metrics
says: Alert evaluation reports AI detector unavailable multiple times for one check
Monitoring dashboard inflates AI detector failure counts during alert retries
Metrics show duplicate unavailable events when alert system retries failed checks
AI detection failures counted per retry attempt instead of per scheduled check
search: The metric posthog_insight_alerts_ai_detector_checks_total{outcome="unavailable"} increments once per scheduled check only when the retry-exhausted path writes an errored check, enforced in posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:record_failed_evaluation by incrementing only when error.get("code") == LLM_DETECTOR_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR_CODE AND an errored check was actually written. The evaluate_alert and _evaluate functions must NOT call record_ai_detector_check_outcome("unavailable") when re-raising LLMDetectorUnavailableError, because a retry that then succeeds would otherwise count both failure and success. Early returns in _record (alert disabled, gone, or next_check_at in future) write no errored check and must not move the counter. Tests test_an_unavailable_detector_is_not_counted_on_every_attempt and test_counts_one_unavailable_outcome_per_recorded_failure in posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_activities.py verify the constraint.
